sections.title: NORTHERN PLAINS
sections.text: MORNING SOUNDINGS CONFIRMS THAT A SUBSTANTIAL EML HAS SPREAD EWD ACROSS THE NORTHERN AND CENTRAL PLAINS...SETTING THE STAGE FOR DEVELOPMENT OF A VERY UNSTABLE AIR MASS THIS AFTERNOON. PWAT GREATER THAN 1.5 INCHES COUPLED WITH DAYTIME HEATING WILL LEAD TO MLCAPES CLIMBING TO ABOVE 3000 J/KG MUCH OF THE PLAINS ALONG AND E OF SURFACE PRESSURE TROUGH AND LOW CENTER. WELL DEFINED LOW CURRENTLY CENTRAL SD WILL MAINTAIN A 30-40 KT SLY LOW LEVEL JET THRU THE DAY WHICH ONCE SURFACE BASED THUNDERSTORMS FORM THIS AFTERNOON. WHILE THE PRIMARY UPPER TROUGH STILL WELL TO THE W...STRONGER SWLY FLOW WITH EMBEDDED IMPULSES HAS SPREAD ACROSS NRN PLAINS AND WILL PROVIDE MORE THAN SUFFICIENT DEEP LAYER SHEAR FOR BOTH ORGANIZED THUNDERSTORMS AND SUPERCELL POTENTIAL. TO THE N AND E OF SURFACE LOW WHICH WILL ONLY SLOWLY MOVE NEWD ACROSS SD TODAY...SHEAR AND INSTABILITY WILL BE MOST FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS INCLUDING LARGE HAIL AND POSSIBLE TORNADOES. BY LATE AFTERNOON SURFACE BASED THUNDERSTORMS SHOULD BE ABLE TO FORM SWD VICINITY AND E OF SURFACE TROUGH AND WITH STEEP LAPSE RATES AND EXPECTED MDT INSTABILITY...PROVIDE A THREAT OF AT LEAST MULTICELL SEVERE. ONE OR MORE MCS/S ARE LIKELY TO DEVELOP BY THIS

sections.title: MID ATLANTIC STATES
sections.text: ON THE SOUTHERN PERIPHERY OF LARGE SCALE HEIGHT FALLS /30-60 M/ PER 12Z 500MB ANALYSIS...A WELL-SUSTAINED SMALL BOWING COMPLEX CONTINUES TO SHOW SOUTHEASTWARD FORWARD ACCELERATION IN VICINITY SRN CHESAPEAKE BAY. WITH A VERY UNSTABLE AND BECOMING VIRTUALLY UNCAPPED AIR MASS VA/NC COASTAL VICINITY...THIS COMPLEX AND ADDITIONAL BACKBUILDING-TYPE DEVELOPMENT EXPECTED TO RESULT IN PRIMARILY A DAMAGING WIND THREAT THROUGH THE AFTERNOON AS COLD POOLS DEVELOP UNDER 30-40KT OF DEEP LAYER SHEAR AND PWAT AOA 2 INCHES. ..HALES/STOPPKOTTE.. 08/12/2010

sections.title: 20Z OUTLOOK UPDATE
sections.text: ADJUSTMENTS TO CATEGORICAL AND PROBABILISTIC OUTLOOK LINES ARE MAINLY AN ATTEMPT TO BETTER ACCOUNT FOR TRENDS IN ONGOING CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT AND DESTABILIZATION.

sections.title: NORTHERN PLAINS INTO UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY
sections.text: DOWNSTREAM OF A REMNANT MID-LEVEL CIRCULATION/IMPULSE BEGINNING TO ACCELERATE EASTWARD OUT OF THE NORTHERN INTERMOUNTAIN REGION... SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ARE POSSIBLE EAST OF THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF THE NORTHERN/CENTRAL ROCKIES THROUGH THE HIGH PLAINS. IN THE PRESENCE OF VERY STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES...THE RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL WILL EXIST. HOWEVER...COVERAGE OF SEVERE STORMS PROBABLY WILL REMAIN RELATIVE SPARSE. THE PRIMARY CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING IS EXPECTED TO BE CONCENTRATED NEAR/NORTH AND EAST OF THE CENTRAL SOUTH DAKOTA SURFACE LOW...WHERE STRONGER LOW-LEVEL FORCING MAY ASSIST IN OVERCOMING LARGE MID-LEVEL INHIBITION ASSOCIATED WITH A BROAD PLUME OF VERY WARM ELEVATED MIXED LAYER WHICH HAS ADVECTED ACROSS THE NORTHERN PLAINS. ADDITIONAL SUSTAINED STORMS ARE POSSIBLE SOUTHWARD ALONG A TRAILING SURFACE TROUGH/DRY LINE INTO CENTRAL/EASTERN NEBRASKA...BUT MID/UPPER FORCING MAY NOT STRENGTHEN ACROSS THIS REGION UNTIL LATE THIS EVENING WITH THE APPROACH OF THE IMPULSE FROM THE INTERMOUNTAIN REGION. THERMODYNAMIC PROFILES CHARACTERIZED BY VERY STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES...HIGH BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE CONTENT...AND LARGE CAPE WILL BE FAVORA
